hypothesis.claim: A shared component-preset cache needs cross-instance/process serialization and lock-held reload; otherwise successful mutations can overwrite one another through stale complete snapshots.
hypothesis.trigger: two catalogs are constructed before either create, or two independent processes create different IDs concurrently
hypothesis.expected_baseline: both mutations return success but a fresh catalog can contain only one ID
hypothesis.expected_candidate: both IDs survive reload; lock contention blocks the writer; malformed reload does not clear the last published in-memory state
hypothesis.falsifier: any successful shared-directory mutation is lost, a writer bypasses an owned lock, or a failed reload clears a previously published definition

implementation: serialize catalog mutations with an in-process RLock plus a stable OS lock file
reload presets.json after acquiring the lock and before validation/mutation
publish parsed reload state only after the entire file has been validated
retain atomic temporary-file write and os.replace
activation_checks: stale-instance reproduction lost one successful ID before the change
two independent Windows processes read back both simultaneous IDs after the change
lock holder blocked a writer until release
malformed reload preserved the previous published catalog state
